text:
Emma (PM): FYI Acme just pushed — they want SOC2 Type II in place within ~8 weeks or they pull the deal. can we sync quickly on tradeoffs between landing SOC2 vs shipping the Q2 roadmap features?
Raj (Eng): ouch. do we have a hard date from them? 8 weeks is tight for Type II.
Ben (Sales): confirmed — procurement said 8 weeks. customer is willing to sign sooner if we show concrete plan + milestone commitments.
Sara (Security): quick notes: SOC2 readiness can be staged. three rough buckets: 1) controls + docs (policies, logging, roles) ~4–6w; 2) remediation (gaps) variable; 3) external audit -> Type II report needs at least 3 months of operating the controls. so full Type II in 8w is unrealistic.
Miguel (Legal): GDPR DPA asks overlap with SOC2 controls (data mapping, subprocessors, retention). we can bundle DPA updates with readiness work.
Olivia (CTO): we need a prioritization framework here. propose: RICE-ish lens for each option (SOC2 readiness path vs feature A/B/C).
Raj (Eng): can we get quick RICE numbers for the two paths? e.g. 
```
Option: SOC2 readiness MVP
Reach: 1 major deal (Acme) + unlock pipeline (5 enterprise prospects)
Impact: 9 (revenue + enterprise growth)
Confidence: 60%
Effort: 6 engineer-weeks (cross-team)
RICE score: (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort ~ (6*9*0.6)/6 = 5.4
```
Olivia (CTO): and for Feature A (conversational rerank):
```
Reach: 1000 MAUs (existing customers)
Impact: 5
Confidence: 80%
Effort: 4 engineer-weeks
RICE score ~ (1000*5*0.8)/4 = 1000 (scale different), normalize by revenue/strategic value instead
```
Emma (PM): numbers look messy because reach is different unit. suggest using normalized business-value units: short term ARR impact + strategic unlock multiplier.
Mei (CS): from CS: enterprise prospects care about SOC2 more than new features. losing Acme is a 6-figure ARR risk.
Ben (Sales): exactly — we have 3 other deals in legal w/ similar asks. this is not one-off.
Sara (Security): tradeoffs: shifting 2 squads for compliance work slows feature velocity; but partial approach: (A) SOC2 readiness MVP (controls + docs) to satisfy procurement + interim DPA + (B) continue low-effort feature work. that reduces risk.
Raj (Eng): what exactly is "SOC2 readiness MVP" scope? list of must-have controls?
Emma (PM): proposed MVP scope (high level):
- access controls & IAM baseline (RBAC, org-only SSO)
- audit logging + retention policy (centralized logs)
- incident response runbook + Slack/RBAC hooks
- basic change control + deploy approvals
- updated DPA + data mapping docs
This is what procurement usually wants to see in an initial commitment.
Miguel (Legal): agree, with note: DPA and subprocessor list need to be editable. offer to draft DPA template within 5 business days.
Olivia (CTO): sequencing options:
1) Full pivot: pause feature work, go all-in on readiness (fastest for controls but high cost)
2) Hybrid: create 2-week "compliance sprint" every 3 weeks and keep feature squads running thinner
3) Parallel: dedicate one small squad to compliance + leverage contractors/audit consultants (costly but fastest)
Which is feasible?
Raj (Eng): hybrid seems least risky. parallel with contractors could hit 8-week milestone but budget hit and onboard time for contractor/auditor.
Ben (Sales): budget is available if it means closing Acme this quarter — they can sign an upfront security/compliance surcharge.
Mei (CS): customers expect a timeline and milestones. can we offer: "SOC2 readiness commitment: controls in 6 weeks, public compliance roadmap, Type II audit scheduled"?
Emma (PM): suggested launch criteria for the customer's procurement acceptance:
- docs: SOC2 policy pack + DPA draft (ready)
- technical: RBAC + SSO + audit logs enabled for their org
- process: IR runbook + monthly compliance check-ins
If we hit these, procurement typically ok to proceed while Type II runs in background.
Sara (Security): note: we must avoid shortcuts that create security debt. any "MVP" must be validated by security review. I can do audits on the deliverables weekly.
Olivia (CTO): decision needed from execs: allow reallocation of 1 infra squad + 1 platform engineer for 6 weeks OR approve contractor budget (~$60k) to accelerate.
Emma (PM): propose immediate steps:
- quick exec sync today 11:30 (I’ll book)
- draft SOC2 MVP scope doc (Emma + Sara + Miguel) by EOD
- Raj to estimate engineer-weeks by EOD
- Ben to confirm Acme willingness to sign with milestones
Raj (Eng): will do. rough estimate: 8 engineer-weeks total but parallelizable to hit must-haves in ~4–6w with 2 FTEs + contractor.
Ben (Sales): Acme confirmed they're OK with milestone-driven signing if we show an internal timeline and weekly updates.
deploy-bot: Deployed branch "soc2-readiness/prototype" to staging at 1716005600
Olivia (CTO): OK. plan for exec sync. main tradeoff: short-term velocity vs revenue risk. leaning toward staged compliance to avoid churn.
Mei (CS): one note — communicate clearly to customers which controls are in and which are pending. transparency reduces churn.
Emma (PM): thanks everyone. action items posted in the thread. we'll capture RICE-like scores in the doc but weight them by ARR risk + strategic unlock. @Olivia I'll add a decision checkbox for contractor budget. :thumbsup:
